images.title: A cycle and two left turns
images.purpose: Show a cycle driving north, turning left to drive west, and turning left again to drive south, so that the turn (left) and the direction (north, west, south) are seen as two different things.
images.composition: An upside down U shaped road drawn from above: up on the right, across the top to the left, down on the left, with a cycle on each of the three parts, three direction tags, two turn tags and a compass card.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. At the top, centred at x 728 and y 60, the heading A cycle and two left turns in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (44 px). ROAD: three rectangles joined into one upside down U, all filled grey #6B7280 with no outline: the right part x 700 to 770 and y 215 to 700; the top part x 410 to 770 and y 215 to 285; the left part x 410 to 480 and y 215 to 700. The road is 70 px wide everywhere, its middle line runs from x 735 and y 700 up to x 735 and y 250, then left to x 445 and y 250, then down to x 445 and y 700. TRAIL: one dashed teal #0072B2 line (6 px thick, dashes 30 px long with 20 px gaps) along that middle line, with three teal arrow heads (24 px): one at x 735 and y 400 pointing up, one at x 590 and y 250 pointing left, one at x 445 and y 400 pointing down. CYCLES: exactly 3 cycle icons, each one amber #E69F00 rounded rectangle 60 by 36 px with a dark #2B2B2B outline (3 px), two small white circles of radius 9 inside it as wheels, and a dark triangle pointer 24 px long at its front end. Cycle 1 on the right part, centred at x 735 and y 560, standing upright 36 px wide by 60 px tall with the pointer at the top (heading up). Cycle 2 on the top part, centred at x 590 and y 250, lying 60 px wide by 36 px tall with the pointer at the left (heading left). Cycle 3 on the left part, centred at x 445 and y 560, standing upright with the pointer at the bottom (heading down). TURN MARKS: two white circles of radius 26 with a dark outline (4 px), one at the first corner centred at x 735 and y 250 and one at the second corner centred at x 445 and y 250. TURN TAGS: each a rounded rectangle 210 by 50 px, white fill, amber #E69F00 outline 5 px, dark bold text (30 px): the tag Left turn 1 at x 800 to 1010 and y 225 to 275, joined by a 3 px dark line from x 800 and y 250 to x 761 and y 250; the tag Left turn 2 at x 185 to 395 and y 225 to 275, joined by a 3 px dark line from x 395 and y 250 to x 419 and y 250. DIRECTION TAGS: each a rounded rectangle 240 by 50 px, white fill, green #009E73 outline 5 px, dark bold text (30 px): the tag driving north at x 800 to 1040 and y 535 to 585; the tag driving west at x 470 to 710 and y 145 to 195; the tag driving south at x 150 to 390 and y 535 to 585. COMPASS: A compass card, a square 110 by 110 px centred at x 1285 and y 155 (x 1230 to 1340, y 100 to 210), white fill, dark #2B2B2B outline 4 px, with N at its top centre, S at its bottom centre and W at its left centre in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (30 px), and E at its right centre in red #D55E00 bold (30 px), and a thin dark cross of two 3 px lines, each 50 px long, centred on the card between the four letters. In all: 1 road, 1 trail, 3 arrow heads, 3 cycles, 2 turn marks, 2 turn tags, 3 direction tags, 1 compass card. No other text and nothing else in the frame.

images.takeaway: A cycle that drives north and turns left drives west, and when it turns left again it drives south.
images.description: An upside down U shaped road seen from above with a cycle driving north, then west after the first left turn, then south after the second left turn, and a compass.
images.context: Concept image for Turning Right and Left on a Route. It follows the idea of the bus route in your maths book (a vehicle turns at junctions and its direction changes) and uses this concept's own example, a cycle that turns left twice.
images.teaching_notes: Let the student say the turn and the direction at each cycle: left turn, now driving west. The slip to watch: saying a turn is a direction, or believing that a turn to the left always means driving west.

image_decisions.why: The road with three cycles shows the turn and the direction side by side, which the words alone do not.
